property_summary: After two calls to SetMinSum before initialization, MinSum must equal either the first value, or the sum of both values.

The reference C keeps MinSum unchanged after Collect (since MinSum is never modified except by SetMinSum), while the buggy version increases MinSum when SetMinSum is called, violating the invariant that MinSum remains constant unless explicitly set during initialization.
After initialization, MinSum remains equal to its initial set value regardless of subsequent calls to SetMinSum or Collect; the buggy version increases MinSum on each SetMinSum call.
MinSum must remain unchanged after initialization; the mutant increases it on each SetMinSum call, so multiple calls make it exceed the initial value.

After initialization, MinSum must always equal the exact value passed to the single allowed SetMinSum call; the mutant adds the argument to MinSum instead, so after a non-zero _val call MinSum will exceed its original value.

After any sequence of calls, MinSum is always exactly one of the values passed to SetMinSum before initialization (or zero), never their sum; the mutant adds the argument to MinSum, so after a non-zero SetMinSum call MinSum exceeds the previous value.
MinSum is immutable after initialization, so a non-zero value set before initialization persists forever

property_summary: SetLogFile reverts only when the contract has been initialized (when Initialized has been called)
SetLogFile reverts if and only if the contract's initialized flag has been set to true.
After initialization, calling SetLogFile again must not change the Log address; the bug allows it to be changed, violating immutability of the logging target.
After initialization, a call to SetLogFile must be ignored and not change the contract's log target, but the buggy version allows it to change the log address.
After initialization, the address returned by the public getter for Log should never change when SetLogFile is called (it stays immutable), but the buggy version allows Log to be updated.
After initialization, the Log contract address must remain immutable; the bug allows SetLogFile to change it after initialization.

After the contract is initialized, the address of the Log contract must never change regardless of repeated calls to SetLogFile, but the buggy version allows SetLogFile to update the Log address after initialization.

After calling SetLogFile with any address, the Log variable in the correct contract equals LogFile(_log), but in the buggy version it equals LogFile(address(0)); thus, any subsequent Log-dependent behavior (e.g., AddMessage during Put) will write to a different storage context, visible via the Log() getter.

After SetLogFile is called with a non-zero address, calling Put will cause a successful Log.AddMessage in the reference contract but revert in the buggy contract because the zero-address LogFile has no code.

After SetLogFile is called with any address, calling Collect with sufficient balance, amount, and unlock time will either revert or not revert; in the correct contract, if it doesn't revert it will emit a Collect log via Log.AddMessage, which can be observed by the History length increment, while in the buggy contract Log is zero and any such call will always revert, so a subsequent call to Put (which logs) will succeed in the correct contract but fail in the buggy contract because Log is zero address.

After calling SetLogFile with any address, a subsequent call to Put must succeed (not revert) because it interacts with Log.AddMessage, which always succeeds when Log is a valid deployed LogFile; in the buggy version, Log is zero and Put reverts.

After initialization and SetLogFile has been called, the address returned by c.Log() must equal the LogFile address set internally; the mutant sets it to address(0) regardless of the parameter, so it violates this equality for any non-zero _log.

If SetLogFile is called before initialization, the reference reverts and does not change the Log variable, whereas the buggy version sets Log before reverting, so after the revert the old Log value is lost and replaced by the new one.

After any call to SetLogFile that does NOT revert (i.e. after initialization), the Log address must equal the argument passed; the buggy version violates this because it also sets Log during reverted pre-initialization calls, overwriting a previously set value with a new one while the reference preserves the old value and reverts.
After a reverted call to SetLogFile before initialization, the Log address must remain unchanged; the buggy version overwrites it before reverting.

After initialization, any successful call to SetLogFile must set Log to the argument; the buggy version can leave Log set to a different address if a pre-initialization reverted call overwrites a previously set Log address.

For any address _log, calling SetLogFile(_log) before initialization always reverts and leaves the Log address unchanged in the reference, but the buggy version overwrites Log with _log before reverting, so after a subsequent successful SetLogFile with a different address, the final Log address differs.

property_summary: A call to Put with a nonpositive _lockTime always reverts.
If _lockTime is zero, the call to Put must revert.
A call to Put with a positive _lockTime never reverts.
A call to c.Put with a positive _lockTime always succeeds and never reverts.

For any account that makes multiple Put calls with different lock times, the unlockTime must be at least as large as the maximum block.timestamp + _lockTime from its Put calls; the bug forces the unlockTime backward to a smaller value, violating this invariant.

After any sequence of calls, a given account's unlockTime must be at least block.timestamp + _lockTime from any past Put call by that account; the mutant unconditionally overwrites unlockTime, possibly setting it to an earlier value.

For any account that has made multiple Put calls, after a Put with _lockTime that would result in an unlock time earlier than the current unlockTime, the unlockTime must remain unchanged; the mutant overwrites it to the smaller value.

After any sequence of calls, an account's unlockTime must be at least the largest of block.timestamp + _lockTime from its past Put calls; the mutant unconditionally overwrites unlockTime, allowing it to be set to a smaller value, which can make Collect succeed earlier than it should.

For any account, after any sequence of calls, the unlockTime must be at least the maximum of block.timestamp + _lockTime from all Put calls by that account; the mutant can reduce unlockTime to an earlier value, allowing premature Collect even when a later Put would have blocked it.
After two Puts, the unlock time can never be less than the maximum of the individual lock times.

property_summary: A user's unlockTime should never decrease via Put, but the buggy condition allows it to be overwritten with an earlier timestamp.

After any sequence of calls to Put and Collect, for every depositor, the stored unlockTime in the Acc mapping must be at least the latest Put's block.timestamp + _lockTime among all their deposits; the buggy contract can set it to an earlier value.
